transcript.text: I want to address the timing interaction that Jonah, Leah, and Marta have flagged. From a legal compliance perspective, the MNPI screening must be completed before any participant can be accepted into the program — that is a precondition to participation, not something that runs in parallel with acceptance. The independent tender administrator will manage the tender process end to end, which means the administrator will handle share tenders, verify MNPI screening clearance, and finalize participation amounts. So the sequence would be: participants submit tenders through the administrator, MNPI screening is completed for each participant, and only then are accepted amounts finalized — at which point pro rata allocation would be applied if oversubscribed. The three-business-day remittance clock should not begin until the administrator has finalized all accepted amounts, including pro rata calculations. Jonah and Marta, this means the remittance window starts after allocation finalization, not at tender submission. I'll make sure the operational safeguards section reflects this sequencing clearly so treasury and tax can assess whether the timeline is feasible.
